segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: You are getting on a Northline ferry next month and you are holding a Harbour card. Does it work?

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: My instinct says yes, because I read that the two of them signed something in January.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Harbour Transit is not on Northline's live interoperability list, and a Harbour card cannot be used to pay a fare on a Northline service as of the twelfth of February 2026.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: So what did they actually sign?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Northline Ferries and the Harbour Transit Authority signed a fare interoperability agreement on the third of January 2026.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: The signed agreement covers forty-two terminals across the two networks.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: Forty-two terminals and no date. That is the part that tells you where this is.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Neither operator has announced a date for passenger availability.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: But I did read that the deal enables Harbour cards on Northline. I am not making that up.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: You are not. Trade reporting describes the January 2026 agreement as enabling Harbour cards to be used for fare payment on Northline coastal services.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Both of those are in the ledger, both marked contested, because one is about what the agreement is for and the other is about what the reader will hit at the gangway.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: And travellers have been finding out the hard way?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Travellers report Harbour cards being declined at the Northline gangway in December 2025 and again in February 2026.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: That one is marked reported rather than checked. A forum thread tells you what people hit. It does not tell you what the scheme supports.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: So what do I do next month?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Paper tickets and cash remain available at every Northline terminal counter and at the quayside machines.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: The same travellers report that Meridian card taps work on the routes they used.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: Cash, a paper ticket, or a Meridian Card. That is ours, not the sources'.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Recheck the operator's live list before you travel. It is the page every moving claim in this episode links to.

Ravi.hint: brighter, faster, asks the blunt question
